answer_1.quote: The aim of data-to-text (D2T) generation is to produce natural language descriptions of structured data .
answer_1.outputs: natural language descriptions of RDF triples

answer_2.quote: We use BLEU and METEOR to evaluate the outputs against the human references. We also evaluate the number of omission and hallucination errors ... using a metric ... based on a RoBERTa model pretrained on natural language inference (NLI).

answer_4.quote: We manually examined 100 outputs of the models. We counted the number of errors: factual (hallucinations, omissions, incorrect fact merging, redundancies) and grammatical.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators counted errors in the generated texts, categorising them as hallucinations, omissions, incorrect fact merging, redundancies, and grammar/disfluency errors.
